short: Spoken-to-imagined EEG transfer (M04) is the standard overt-to-covert design; 26.8% vs 30.5% on 5 classes, no chance level, and "comparable" rests on a non-significant omnibus test.
position: The paper [@lee2022towards] changes the use-time action (M04, with M01 and M03): imagined-speech EEG is classified by a CSP+SVM model trained on the same participants' spoken-speech EEG. The design is standard: 25 confirmed studies apply an overt-trained decoder to silent or covert speech, 9 of them prior, Martin et al. for covert speech in ECoG [@martin2014] (Appendix), and Rekrut et al. ran it in EEG [concurrent] [@rekrut2022improving]. The transfer stays below the imagined-speech baseline, 26.8% against 30.5% on five classes and lower in 5 of 7 subjects (Table I), and 10 spoken trials per class do better (28.0%) than all trials. "Comparable performance" (§III.A) rests on a non-significant omnibus Kruskal–Wallis test over seven subjects, with no equivalence test and no chance level (M12). The claim that imagined speech is closer to spoken speech than visual imagery fails: transfer reaches 26.8% on imagined speech and 26.3% on visual imagery (Tables I–II); only the baselines differ.
